title: Dataq Ledger — Overview
meta_description: Shared truth with regulatory teeth — permissioned networks that survive supervision.

blocks.x: A no-theater description of Dataq Ledger — Overview: what ships first, what it touches at operational stores, how it is verified, and the per workflow metric we commit to moving against baseline.

Dataq Ledger is the institution-grade DLT platform: permissioned network engineering (Fabric/Besu-class) with governance charters and legal wrappers, tokenization with securities-law discipline, smart contracts built to formal-verification standards, provenance networks for EUDR/DPP-grade traceability, and verifiable-credential ecosystems against eIDAS 2.0 expectations.

blocks.x: What holds the build together is discipline at the boundaries: identity is short-lived and authorization is deny-by-default in Data, Analytics & Lakehouse delivery, which is what makes the reported delta defensible in audit.

Ledger leads with governance because networks fail on governance, not cryptography: membership rules, data-visibility zones, key custody under HSM, and regulator packs — privacy model, audit exports, jurisdiction analysis — shipped with every network.
